results.reasoning: Driven with Playwright against the panel on port 4713 over the throwaway expenses rig (serve 4701, app 4737 local / 4738 review), tree 7bf1cfdc-dirty, panel build c2158b76c95a. Step 1: on 6 of 6 fresh panels started on /expenses/7, opening org-note, team-no-approve or team-note ran the setup, landed on /expenses/412 as user 31 or 14, panel.screen-picker named that rule's screen, panel.screen-tied was absent and panel.screens-list stayed hidden, sampled every 60ms from the click and again 3s after; the same held when going from one tied screen's rule to the other's in one panel, after switching panel.target to review (user 77 / 31 on /expenses/9 on :4738) and back, and across a walkdown stepping team-note then org-note. So the n-0633 behaviour did not occur in any of roughly 20 openings. Six pins placed after opening org-note were filed with screen expense-org and rule expenses.view.org-note, and six after team-no-approve with expense-team, read from the POST response and the thread files (since removed from the rig). Step 2: a fresh tab on /expenses/412 opened the picker by itself with the bar reading 'Which screen?', the note 'Two screens share /expenses/412...', two rows with each screen's setup in words, and 'Picking one runs its setup here. Nothing is filed under either until you do.'; Pin mode was disabled with the title 'Pick a screen first, so the pin is filed under the right one', the app log showed no request and the threads folder stayed empty. The same happened on review's address /expenses/9 once review was the chosen target, with review's fixture (user_id 77) in the row. Step 3: picking the org row asked the app POST /dev/session (user_id 31) then GET /expenses/412; the team row asked GET /dev/impersonate?id=1, POST /dev/session (14), GET /expenses/412: the same requests opening the rule makes. The menu shut, the bar named the screen and Pin mode came back. With the POST held five seconds the bar read the picked screen's title throughout, never 'Which screen?', and the menu was shut, whether the setup came from a tied row, from the ordinary list row, or from a rule opened while the question was showing. Closed with Escape, the question did not reopen in 4s, the bar kept 'Which screen?' and Pin mode stayed disabled; reopened by hand it showed the two rows again and stayed open. A menu opened by hand on /expenses/7 and on a set-up tied screen stayed open for 3s. Step 4: the rig has no such pair, so I imported a copy of the expenses blueprint with two extra screens at /expenses/55 sharing one recipe into a home of its own under the session scratchpad, served it on 4742 with the fixture app on 4743, and took it down afterwards. Lint warned 'app path /expenses/55 and setup { recipe: as_view_only_org_manager } are both screen expense-twin-a's - a tie is never matched...' and did not warn about expense-team and expense-org. The panel did not ask there: it took the first, and with twin-b's rule open it said 'This rule is on expense-twin-b; you are on expense-twin-a', which is the ordinary tie the step says remains; twin-b was reachable by picking it by hand. Edges weighed, none filed. If the question is dismissed and panel.target is then switched to review, the frame stays on local's /expenses/412, the bar reads 'No screen' and Pin mode is enabled, so a pin could be filed under no screen: about 5%, since it needs a person to refuse the question and change target before picking. Pin mode is enabled while a tied screen's setup is still running, about a second in practice: under 5% and the pin would go under the screen being set up. One pin placement out of twelve hung in my script before the form appeared and did not recur in eleven further tries; I could not tie it to this rule. Remaining departures from the accepted design in the tied state: the note sits above the ordinary list (redlined), and the Design and App buttons are dimmed where the drawing shows them plain.
